modelAnswer: The Lucknow Pact brought Congress and the Muslim League together in 1916. Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims and one-third Muslim representation in the central council. modelAnswer: The Khilafat Movement developed after Turkey, the seat of the Khilafat, was defeated in the First World War and the Ottoman institution came under threat. Indian Muslims organized it to safeguard the Khilafat. Its primary objectives were that the Turkish Khilafat should not be abolished, Muslim sacred places should not be disrespected, and the territories held by Turkey before the war should not be taken away. The movement later failed, but it increased Muslim political confidence and maturity.

modelAnswer: The Nehru Report was prepared by an all-party committee headed by Motilal Nehru in 1928. It proposed joint electorates instead of separate electorates, reserved one-fourth of the central legislative assembly seats for Muslims, separation of Sindh, greater powers for Balochistan and the North West Frontier Province, and Hindi as the official language. Muslim members rejected it because it ignored Muslim interests and reversed important safeguards accepted in the Lucknow Pact.

modelAnswer: The Simla Conference of 1945 failed because Quaid-e-Azam insisted that all five Muslim members of the executive council should be nominated by the Muslim League, which he regarded as the sole representative of Indian Muslims. Khizar Hayat wanted one Muslim seat for his Unionist Party, and Congress supported that demand while also claiming to represent Muslims. The disagreement created a deadlock and the conference ended without agreement.

modelAnswer: The Cabinet Mission Plan proposed an Indian union of British India and the princely states, with the centre controlling defence, foreign affairs, communications, and taxation. Provinces would be arranged into three groups: Hindu-majority Group A, Punjab, Sindh and NWFP in Group B, and Bengal and Assam in Group C. Provinces retained powers over subjects outside the union list and residuary powers, and a province could consider secession after ten years. Parties had to accept or reject the plan as a whole.

modelAnswer: The Lahore Resolution demanded that geographically contiguous Muslim-majority areas in the north-western and eastern zones of India should be grouped into independent states, with constituent units that were autonomous and sovereign. It rejected a constitutional plan based on the assumption that India was one nation and provided the political basis for a separate Muslim homeland.

modelAnswer: The 3rd June Plan provided that the Sindh Assembly would decide whether Sindh would join India or Pakistan, a referendum would be held in NWFP, and the Punjab and Bengal legislatures would decide their futures. Sylhet would hold a referendum, Balochistan's royal jirga and Quetta Municipal Corporation would decide their future, the Government of India Act 1935 would serve as the interim constitution, and princely states would choose their own future.
